text: For a smallholder farmer in Preah Vihear, cattle housing should provide adequate space, clean drinking water, suitable feeding areas, shade/weather protection, safe footing, drainage, and reasonable ventilation — a simple roofed shelter with good airflow can be more practical than an enclosed building, and ventilation should not be sacrificed for enclosure in Cambodia's hot climate. During the wet season (roughly May–October), heavy rain can turn areas muddy and contaminate feeding/watering points, so drainage and a dry resting area are priorities. During the dry season (roughly November–April), heat, dust, and limited water matter more, so shade, airflow, and reliable clean water should be prioritized. Biosecurity means reducing opportunities for disease entry/spread: obtain cattle from sources with known health history, avoid visibly sick animals, keep newly purchased cattle separate from the herd for a veterinarian-guided observation period before mixing, and separate sick animals promptly. Shared grazing, communal water, livestock markets, transport, visitors, and shared equipment are all disease-transmission opportunities that cannot always be eliminated — the practical priorities are clean water, drainage, shade, controlled animal introductions, temporary isolation of new/sick cattle, cleaning shared equipment, and reducing unnecessary animal contact. No specific cattle breed is claimed as predominant in Preah Vihear without reliable evidence — record the farmer's actual cattle type.
